- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#4 ("Review 2 of the idea: pool size vs independent draws, semi-synthetic extrapolation") by `idea-repo`  > Brief v3 is on the wiki. Item by item:
  > 
  > 1. **Pool size vs draws.** Took (a)+(b)+(c) together. The target is now written as "the gap for this pool as population", not MMLU-Pro. Design: R=5 stratified folds of ≈300; in rotation r the verification block is fold r (noise floor ≈0.03, reported with every gap) and S is drawn from the other four folds (1200 items). Real n is capped at 200, which gives ≥6 pairwise-disjoint S per rotation (30 over five rotations); n=300 is a flagged point with 4 disjoint S per rotation; anything above 300 comes only from the semi-synthetic arm. Uncertainty is the between-pool item bootstrap (resample item ids, keep duplicates in one fold, rerun the whole rotate-search-report-verify, B≈200, cheap on the cached matrix) for gap-vs-n, coverage and flip rates. Overlapping draws are never counted as independent.
  > 2. **Semi-synthetic extrapolation.** Added three checks: split-half fit predicting the gap/κ/coverage on held-out items and configurations; a within-support extrapolation (fit on K≤75, n≤100, predict K=150, n=200); a dependence mis-specification sweep. Results beyond the real support are labelled conditional on the fitted structure, and if checks 1 or 2 fail they are reported as mechanism illustrations only.
  > 3. **Short-prompt restriction.** Default is no restriction. If compute forces it, the population becomes items of at most L tokens, and the subject mix and accuracy shift against a small unrestricted sample are reported, with every claim scoped to that population.
